title: The Weight of Abstract Ideas
text:
Abstract nouns such as freedom, justice, and integrity name ideas rather than physical objects. Because they cannot be seen or touched, writers rely on concrete examples to make them understandable. A scholar who discusses justice, for instance, usually anchors the argument in a particular court case.

The same abstraction can also cause confusion. Two readers may agree that a society values fairness yet disagree sharply about what fairness requires in practice. Careful academic writing therefore defines its key abstract nouns early and returns to those definitions consistently. Without this discipline, the argument becomes vague and difficult to assess.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what do abstract nouns name?
options: Physical objects that can be touched

questions.text: What does careful academic writing do with its key abstract nouns, according to the second paragraph?
options: It defines them early and returns to those definitions
It replaces them with slang terms
It uses them only in the conclusion

questions.text: Why does the author suggest that writers use concrete examples?
options: Because abstract ideas are impossible to discuss
Because readers may struggle to grasp ideas they cannot see or touch
Because concrete examples are always shorter
Because court cases are the only valid evidence

questions.text: What does the author imply can happen when abstract nouns are left undefined?
options: Readers always reach the same understanding
The argument can become vague and hard to evaluate
Editors remove the abstract nouns automatically

vocabulary.definition: existing as an idea rather than as a physical thing
specific and real, based on actual facts or examples
a controlled, consistent way of working or thinking

paragraph_translations: Rzeczowniki abstrakcyjne, takie jak wolność, sprawiedliwość i uczciwość, nazywają idee, a nie przedmioty fizyczne. Ponieważ nie można ich zobaczyć ani dotknąć, autorzy polegają na konkretnych przykładach, aby były zrozumiałe. Badacz omawiający sprawiedliwość zwykle opiera swój wywód na konkretnej sprawie sądowej.

Ta sama abstrakcja może też prowadzić do nieporozumień. Dwaj czytelnicy mogą zgadzać się, że społeczeństwo ceni sprawiedliwość, a mimo to ostro spierać się o to, czego ona wymaga w praktyce. Dlatego staranne pisanie akademickie definiuje kluczowe rzeczowniki abstrakcyjne na początku i konsekwentnie wraca do tych definicji. Bez tej dyscypliny argument staje się niejasny i trudny do oceny.
